title: Your Heart Beats 100,000 Times a Day ❤️ #shorts

beats.vo: Your heart beats about one hundred thousand times. Every. Single. Day.
That's more than two and a half billion beats in a lifetime.
Every day, it pushes around seven thousand liters of blood through your body.
And it has never taken a single day off. Follow Inside Human for more.

hook: Why doesn't your stomach digest ITSELF?
title: Why Doesn't Your Stomach Digest Itself? 🤯 #shorts

beats.vo: Your stomach acid is so strong, it could damage your own stomach.
So why doesn't your stomach digest itself?
A thick layer of mucus coats the stomach wall, like a living shield.
And the cells of the lining are replaced every few days.
Your stomach is rebuilding itself right now. Follow Inside Human for more.

hook: What happens when you cut your finger
title: What Your Body Does in Seconds When You Cut Yourself 🩸 #shorts

beats.vo: Cut your finger, and your body launches an emergency repair in seconds.
First, the blood vessel squeezes tight to slow the bleeding.
Then tiny cells called platelets rush in and stick together, forming a plug.
Finally, a protein called fibrin weaves a mesh, and the wound is sealed.
All of that, without you even noticing. Follow Inside Human for more.

hook: Your blood vessels could circle the Earth
title: Your Blood Vessels Could Wrap Around Earth Twice 🌍 #shorts

beats.vo: If you laid out every blood vessel in one adult body, end to end...
they would stretch around one hundred thousand kilometers.
That's enough to circle the Earth more than twice.
Most of it is capillaries, thinner than a human hair. Follow Inside Human for more.

title: Mount Everest Would Disappear in the Mariana Trench 😱 #shorts

beats.vo: If you dropped Mount Everest into the deepest part of the ocean...
its peak would still be more than two kilometers underwater.
That place is the Challenger Deep, in the Mariana Trench.
Down there, the pressure is over a thousand times stronger than at the surface.
Follow Ocean Secrets for more.

title: The Kraken Is Real: The Giant Squid 🦑 #shorts

beats.vo: For centuries, sailors told stories of a sea monster called the Kraken.
The real one exists. The giant squid can grow longer than a bus.
Its eyes are as big as dinner plates, among the largest of any animal.
Its only real enemy? The sperm whale.
Nobody filmed one alive in the deep until 2012. Follow Ocean Secrets for more.

hook: The loudest mystery in the ocean
title: The Bloop: The Ocean's Loudest Mystery 🔊 #shorts

beats.vo: In 1997, underwater microphones caught a sound so loud, it was heard across thousands of kilometers.
Scientists called it... the Bloop.
For years, people believed it came from a giant, unknown creature.
The real answer? Icequakes. Huge icebergs cracking apart near Antarctica.
The ocean was literally breaking. Follow Ocean Secrets for more.

title: Where Sunlight Dies in the Ocean 🌑 #shorts

beats.vo: Dive past two hundred meters, and sunlight begins to fade.
Below one thousand meters, there's no sunlight at all. Total darkness.
Yet the dark is full of light. Most deep sea animals make their own glow.
It's called bioluminescence. Follow Ocean Secrets for more.

hook: The free kick that broke physics
title: The Free Kick That Broke Physics ⚽ Roberto Carlos 1997 #shorts

beats.vo: Nineteen ninety seven. Roberto Carlos steps up against France.
The ball flies way wide of the wall...
then bends back like magic, straight into the net.
That's the Magnus effect. Spin makes the air push the ball sideways.
Physicists even wrote a scientific paper about it. Follow Ninetymins!

title: Why Knuckleball Shots Wobble 🤯 Football Physics #shorts

beats.vo: Ever seen a shot swerve left, then right, and fool the keeper completely?
That's a knuckleball, struck with almost no spin.
With no spin, the air around the ball keeps shifting.
So it wobbles unpredictably. Even the shooter can't control it. Follow Ninetymins!

title: How Far Does a Footballer Run in One Match? 🏃 #shorts

beats.vo: How far does a pro footballer run in one match?
About ten to thirteen kilometers.
Midfielders usually run the most, and players sprint dozens of times.
That's a quarter marathon, while fighting for the ball. Follow Ninetymins!

title: World Cup 2026 Made History 🏆 By the Numbers #shorts

beats.vo: The 2026 World Cup was the biggest in history.
Forty eight teams, up from thirty two.
One hundred and four matches.
Three host countries. The USA, Canada and Mexico, across sixteen cities.
And fans everywhere went wild. Follow Ninetymins!
